Finding functions and inspecting results

Source: vignettes/function-naming.Rmd
function-naming.Rmd

The guides use the bundled Cornwall GP data, described in The Cornwall GP example data; this page needs no data.

library(spax)

spax retains its public FCA functions alongside the experimental static allocation workflow. Names describe the interface they belong to; there is no rule that every complete workflow must start with spax_. Existing FCA calls and result types remain supported. Within the allocation workflow, model declarations are named <model>_allocation() (clm_allocation(), huff_allocation()) and workflow steps <verb>_allocation().

Choose the level of operation

Task Public interface What it returns
Binary catchment FCA spax_2sfca() spax result with accessibility raster
Distance-weighted FCA spax_e2sfca() spax result with accessibility raster
Squared access-side decay FCA spax_m2sfca() spax result with accessibility raster
Selection-weighted FCA spax_3sfca(), spax_huff2sfca() spax result with accessibility raster
Supply/demand calculation using supplied kernels compute_access() Accessibility SpatRaster
Decay, normalization or choice weights calc_decay(), decay_kernel(), calc_normalize(), calc_choice() See the individual input/output contracts
Weighted reduction to facilities gather_weighted(), gather_demand() Facility vector/table
Weighted distribution to origins spread_weighted(), spread_access() Raster result
Checked allocation preparation and declaration prepare_allocation(), clm_allocation(), huff_allocation() Prepared inputs and experimental model
Fit, evaluate, predict and bootstrap fit_allocation(), evaluate_allocation(), predict_allocation(), bootstrap_allocation() Model-specific saved results
Check and compare fitted allocations check_allocation(), compare_allocations() Comparison tables; the fits are not changed
Travel times and demand inputs calc_travel_time(), calc_demand() Travel matrix or raster; demand raster or vector

These function families share concepts such as supply, demand and facility IDs. Their arguments and result meanings are not interchangeable. In particular, calc_normalize() applied to a numeric matrix normalizes the whole matrix, whereas a multilayer raster is normalized across layers at each cell. Select the operation appropriate to the declared axes; do not infer behavior from a name.

functions <- c(
  # FCA accessibility
  "spax_2sfca", "spax_e2sfca", "spax_m2sfca", "spax_3sfca", "spax_huff2sfca",
  "compute_access",
  # Experimental allocation workflow
  "prepare_allocation", "clm_allocation", "huff_allocation", "fit_allocation",
  "evaluate_allocation", "predict_allocation", "bootstrap_allocation",
  "check_allocation", "compare_allocations",
  # Input helpers
  "calc_travel_time", "calc_demand", "decay_kernel"
)

# Every name above is exported by the installed package
stopifnot(all(functions %in% getNamespaceExports("spax")))
data.frame(function_name = functions)
          function_name
1            spax_2sfca
2           spax_e2sfca
3           spax_m2sfca
4            spax_3sfca
5        spax_huff2sfca
6        compute_access
7    prepare_allocation
8        clm_allocation
9       huff_allocation
10       fit_allocation
11  evaluate_allocation
12   predict_allocation
13 bootstrap_allocation
14     check_allocation
15  compare_allocations
16     calc_travel_time
17          calc_demand
18         decay_kernel

The former iterative-FCA interface is no longer available. It is not an alias for static CLM or a supported fixed-point workflow. Private functions beginning with . and other unexported implementation functions are not public contracts; examples for users should not call them with :::.

Inspect saved results using standard R generics

Result Inspection Interpretation
FCA spax object print(), summary(), plot(), $accessibility Saved supply-per-demand index; raster-cell summary
Allocation multistart fit coef(), fitted(), summary(), as.data.frame(type = "parameters"), plot() Selected fit plus retained per-start diagnostics
Allocation coverage summary(), as.data.frame(type = "regional") or type = "cells" Saved coverage on retained positive-demand support
Allocation bootstrap summary(), as.data.frame(type = "estimates"), "draws", "starts", plot() Saved point/interval status and every attempted result

Inspection does not refit the allocation model or resample the bootstrap. A failed search can still be summarized, but parameter extraction requires an eligible selected fit. Bootstrap methods preserve incomplete and refused statuses; displaying a point estimate does not make an interval available.

FCA rasters and allocation numeric tables have different storage contracts. Use terra::as.data.frame() to extract raster cell values, and preserve geometry separately. Allocation tables carry IDs; coverage tables also carry unit, support and reporting attributes. CSV loses those attributes, so retain the documented RDS bundle when exporting allocation results.

Keep input validation enabled

Some legacy functions expose snap. Leave its default FALSE in ordinary user code. It is an internal optimization switch, not a different model or a general speed recommendation. New prepared allocation inputs validate IDs, geometry and support at their own boundary and do not use a universal snap convention.

See Choosing an FCA index or an allocation model for a runnable comparison, The E2SFCA calculation step by step for public building blocks, the allocation workflow for fitting, prediction, scenarios and persistence, and Bootstrap intervals for a fitted allocation model for intervals.
